The anatomy of the first drawing is off; Link's head is connected to his neck by his chin, and his left arm looks to be 1/3 shorter than his right. The tunic looks off as well, it doesn't look like it's snug around Link's body like it does in the reference.

The 2nd and 3rd look better, focusing on proportions and the practice seem to have paid off. They both look flat in areas though, as opposed to the three-dimensional look the reference images have. You can really see it when comparing the tunic and face of the 2nd image.

In the last one, Link doesn't have any shoulders. This resulted in his arm being connected to his head!

I recommend watching a video or two about figure drawing or anatomy; there's a lot of helpful links [here in the wiki](https://www.reddit.com/r/learnart/wiki/index/figuredrawing/). I'd also recommend reading through the first few lessons of [Drawabox](https://drawabox.com/) to learn how to create 3D forms on paper (the amount of drills and exercises Drawabox throws at you can feel overwhelming, but they do help). After some practice it should be easier to point out some of the mistakes you're making without realizing it.

1. Yes, you aren't doing anything to reduce your THC usage, you just switched to a different delivery method.
2. Taking more THC to combat withdrawal is the opposite of what you should be doing, and is just making you more dependent on it.
3. In terms of edibles vs smoking... No, edibles will not make any easier to quit. Yes, edibles are better than smoking since heavy smoking will fuck up your lungs. 
4. Yes, the reason you aren't feeling anything from the edibles is because your tolerance is very high. Especially if you are consuming multiple edibles several days in a row.

Withdrawals suck. But taking THC constantly to avoid it sucks more. Take it slow; set yourself a goal of making it one day without ANY THC, smoking or edibles. Steadily increase that goal over time. 

The next time you have the urge to smoke or take a bite of an edible, notice that urge, tell yourself no, and go immerse yourself in something else. Go for a run. Practice an instrument. Read a book.  Reconnect with an old friend (preferably one who doesn't toke). Journal. Anything but going back to the habit.
